samples.text:
With the growth of online shopping and internet banking, the number of online fraud and identity theft cases is increasing. This essay will discuss the problems this situation causes and some measures that can protect people.

The most obvious problem is that people lose their money. For example, a criminal can steal someone's bank details from a fake website and then use them to buy things or take money from the account. Some victims lose all their savings and it is very difficult to get it back. Another problem is stress. When someone's identity is stolen, criminals can open new accounts or take loans in their name, and the victim have to spend months to solve the problem with banks and police. Also, because of these crimes, many people especially older people are afraid to use the internet, so they cannot enjoy the benefits of online services.

There are several measures that can be taken. First of all, banks and online shops should use stronger security, for example sending a code to the customer's phone every time they make a payment. Secondly, people need to be more careful. They should not click on links in strange emails, and they should use different password for different websites. The government and banks can teach people about these dangers through advertisements and short courses, especially for elderly people. Finally, the police need more special officers who understand technology, so they can catch the criminals and punish them strongly.

In conclusion, online fraud cause financial loss, stress and fear of using internet. I believe that better security, public education and stronger police action can help to protect people from this crime.

samples.text:
As more people rely on the internet for shopping and banking, criminals have found increasingly sophisticated ways to steal money and personal data. This essay will discuss the main problems created by online fraud and identity theft and suggest measures that could offer better protection.

The most direct consequence is financial loss. Victims may find that money has been taken from their accounts or that purchases have been made using their card details, and although banks sometimes refund these losses, this is not always the case, especially when the customer has been tricked into authorising a payment themselves. Identity theft can be even more damaging, since criminals may use stolen personal information to open accounts or take out loans in the victim's name, which can harm their credit record for years. Beyond the financial harm, these crimes causes considerable anxiety, and some people, particularly the elderly, may lose confidence in using online services altogether.

Protecting the public requires action from businesses, governments and individuals. Banks and online retailers should continue to strengthen security, for instance through two-factor authentication and systems that detect unusual spending patterns and block suspicious transactions. At the same time, awareness campaigns are essential, because many scams succeed not by breaking technology but by deceiving people. Teaching users to recognise fake emails, avoid sharing passwords and check website addresses would prevent a large number of crimes. Governments, meanwhile, should ensure that police forces have specialist cybercrime units and should cooperate internationally, as many fraudsters operate from other countries.

In conclusion, online fraud and identity theft lead to financial losses, long-term difficulties and a loss of trust in digital services. Stronger security, better public awareness and effective law enforcement together offer the best protection.
samples.why: Clear position · financial and personal problems extended with explanation · measures grouped logically by responsibility · good topic vocabulary (two-factor authentication, cybercrime units) · mostly error-free with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The convenience of online shopping and banking has come at a price: as more of our financial lives move onto digital platforms, fraudsters and identity thieves have found ever more opportunities to exploit them. The resulting harm extends well beyond individual losses, and countering it requires coordinated effort from institutions, governments and users themselves.

The immediate damage is financial. Victims may see their savings drained or discover purchases made with cloned card details, and while banks often reimburse unauthorised transactions, those who were manipulated into making a payment themselves may receive nothing. Identity theft can be more insidious still. Using stolen personal information, criminals can open accounts, apply for credit or commit further offences in another person's name, leaving the victim to spend months restoring their financial reputation. The psychological toll is also significant; many victims describe feelings of violation and shame, and some withdraw from online services entirely. At a societal level, widespread fraud erodes trust in digital commerce and imposes substantial costs on businesses, which are ultimately passed on to consumers.

Because modern fraud targets both systems and people, protection must address both. Financial institutions should adopt robust authentication, such as one-time codes and biometric checks, alongside monitoring systems that flag anomalous transactions in real time. Regulators can reinforce this by requiring companies to meet minimum security standards and to compensate customers fairly when those standards fail. Yet technology alone cannot stop a victim from being persuaded to hand over details voluntarily. Sustained public education, particularly aimed at older and less experienced users, is therefore vital in teaching people to recognise phishing messages and pressure tactics. Finally, since many fraud networks operate across borders, police forces need specialist expertise and effective international cooperation to pursue offenders.

In conclusion, online fraud inflicts financial, psychological and economic damage. Combining secure technology, sensible regulation, public awareness and international enforcement offers the most credible defence.
samples.why: Sufficiently addresses both parts with well-developed ideas at personal and societal levels · solutions tied logically to the nature of the problem · wide, precise vocabulary (insidious, anomalous transactions) · virtually error-free complex structures.
